root_cause.text: An off-by-one boundary error in OCFS2 DLM’s `dlm_match_regions()` comparison loop used `<= qr->qr_numregions` instead of `< qr->qr_numregions`, allowing the code to access one element past the valid `qr_regions` array range.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `for (j = 0; j <= qr->qr_numregions; ++j)` to `for (j = 0; j < qr->qr_numregions; ++j)` in `fs/ocfs2/dlm/dlmdomain.c`, and the commit message states the local-vs-remote region comparison loop was “read[ing] one entry past the valid range of qr_regions.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix an off-by-one error in region matching to prevent out-of-bounds iteration.
intent_record.what: The inner loop condition in dlm_match_regions() was changed from `j <= qr->qr_numregions` to `j < qr->qr_numregions`, so the loop now iterates over exactly `qr->qr_numregions` entries instead of one extra iteration.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents the function from reading and comparing one region past the end of the valid remote region array, avoiding an out-of-bounds access and any incorrect match that could result from examining invalid memory.

candidates.rationale: This loop uses an inclusive upper bound, so when j equals qr->qr_numregions it iterates one past the last valid region element, causing out-of-bounds access in the region-matching logic.

    heartbeat regions. This message is only sent in the global heartbeat
    mode. If the regions in the joining node do not fully match the ones in
    the active nodes, the join domain request is rejected.
    
    Signed-off-by: Sunil
